assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: finished panoramic scene artwork for a gentle coastal learning-app theme. This is only a background illustration, never an app screenshot.
Primary request: a complete wide 16:9 landscape, a warm sunny coastal wooden pier leading diagonally from the lower foreground into a translucent turquoise sea, with distant bright green islands and an open pale-blue sky with softly painted cream clouds. The scene is called Dawn Pier, but do not write its name.
Style/medium: exquisite 2D hand-painted Japanese-animation background art, fine painterly foliage and wave details, gentle light watercolor-gouache texture. Warm airy seaside atmosphere, not 3D and not photorealism. Match the feeling of a cream-colored sunny Mediterranean coastal window painting with turquoise water and ivory highlights.
Composition: true panoramic 16:9 canvas, ideally 1536 by 864 or 2048 by 1152. Clearly readable depth with textured pale wood in the foreground, the pier as the quiet focal shape in the middle distance, sparkling open water and small distant islands. Horizon around the upper third. Keep important details comfortably within the central 80 percent; all four edges have safe margin. The image must remain coherent when displayed at 354 by 199 or 435 by 245 pixels. A few soft coastal grasses near the bottom corners can naturally frame the pier. Use balanced visual breathing room, not empty abstract blocks.
Palette and light: clear turquoise and aqua water, soft sky blue, warm pale cream sunlight, sunlit light honey wood, gentle sage-green foliage. Soft shadows, lively yet calm, refined lightness.
Constraints: one complete landscape image only. No lighthouse, no sea cliff overlook, no bookshop, no interior, no dark starry sky. No people, no human figures, no whale girl, no whales, no animals, no birds, no character, no mascot, no face or avatar. No text, typography, numbers, letters, logo, watermark, border, UI, button, card, device, or mockup. No 3D, plastic surfaces or camera lens effects. Do not crop a portrait composition to make a banner.
